title: Fourteen Springs and One Short Curtain
subtitle: 戏剧表演 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）
meta: 主题语境：戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）　|　核心词汇：drama　|　正文 343 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 drama 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1954 my teacher ① staged a drama that no parent in the hall would have watched, and he said the staging was the whole of the spring. The ② drama, meaning the play and not the scene, ran fourteen springs and stayed unnamed in the book; a drama, he said, is the only thing in a hall that is judged by how long it is left unwatched.

Every ③ drama in that hall had the same short curtain at the side of it, and the ④ drama at the end, meaning the one they kept for the graduating class and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A drama, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to watch; my teacher said the watching is the part that fills fourteen springs.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the drama was the whole of the story, meaning the scene and not the play. The ⑥ drama, meaning the scene and not any of that, is the only thing in a story that everybody talks about and nobody forgets; drama, he said, is either something you stage or the only word that means both a play and a scene. He said the scene is the part they remember.

By 1963 the ⑦ drama had become a line in a programme, and the programme had become an argument about the short curtain. The ⑧ drama of the whole thing, my teacher wrote in April, was one hall and fourteen springs of watching; drama, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to watch. She said the watching was never mentioned.

The ⑨ drama I remember is the one named in the programme, which closed in 1975 and is still described as the quietest in the hall. A ⑩ drama, my mother said in 1977, is the only one that improves by being watched; every drama, she said, is a scene that has agreed to look like a play. She said the scene was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 戏；剧（指那座礼堂里演过的那一出）
B. n. 戏；剧（指那出戏本身，与戏剧性场面相对）
C. 固定搭配：stage a drama 上演一出戏
D. n. 戏；剧（指留给毕业班的那出）
E. n. 戏；剧（抽象总称，指一所学校的演剧之事）
F. n. 戏；剧（指节目单上写到、被列名的那一出）
G. n. 戏剧性场面；风波（指故事里人人议论却无人忘怀的那样事情）
H. n. 戏剧性场面（抽象总称，指人人议论却无人忘怀的那种事情）

items.q: staged a drama that no parent in the hall would have watched
The drama, meaning the play and not the scene
the drama was the whole of the story
the drama had become a line in a programme
The drama of the whole thing
A drama, my mother said in 1977

answers.why: stage a drama 意为“上演一出戏”，1954 年老师上演了一出礼堂里没有一位家长肯去看的戏。
drama 意为“戏、剧”，指那出戏本身而不是戏剧性场面，它经过了十四个春天而在簿子上没有名字。
drama 意为“戏、剧”，指那座礼堂里的每一出戏，每一出侧边都有同一道短短的幕布。
drama 意为“戏、剧”，指留给毕业班的那出，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
drama 意为“戏剧性场面、风波”，指故事里人人议论却无人忘怀的那样事情，叔叔说这场风波就是那个故事的全部。
drama 意为“戏剧性场面”，指人人议论却无人忘怀的那种事情而不是那出戏，是故事里人人都议论、却无人忘怀的东西。
drama 意为“戏、剧”，指节目单上写到、被列名的那一出，到 1963 年这出戏成了节目单里的一行。
drama 意为“戏、剧”，老师四月写道，整件事的演剧之事是一座礼堂和十四个春天的观看。
drama 意为“戏、剧”，我记得的是节目单上列名的那一出，1975 年停演了，至今仍被说成礼堂里最安静的一出。
drama 为抽象总称，母亲 1977 年说，一出戏是唯一会因为被好好观看而变得更好的东西。
